R1_is_the_routing_measurement_architectu.objection: The headline is that deleting layer-0 attention from layer-1's READ costs vanilla 5e-6 nats and the variants 0.07-0.15 -- a factor of 2e4. But the two deletions are not the same intervention. The measurement itself records the displacement it causes: the read moves by 0.2-0.3% in vanilla and by 60-68% in every variant. KL is quadratic in a small displacement, so a 210x displacement ratio predicts a ~4e4 KL ratio ON ITS OWN, with no routing difference whatsoever. As stated, 'the plain model shuts the path and every variant opens it' may be a restatement of 'the per-slot norm forces layer-0 attention's write to be a quarter of the read'.
R1_is_the_routing_measurement_architectu.measurement_proposed_and_run: A MATCHED-DISPLACEMENT DIRECTIONAL PROBE, in the model's own post-norm read space so no normalisation convention enters. For each arm: take layer 1's true normalised read hn; take the direction that upstream module X contributes to it, d_X = hn - norm(stream - X); displace the read by exactly eps*||hn|| along the unit d_X (eps = 5/10/20%, identical in every arm); recompute everything downstream and score the KL. Reference directions: M0 (the other upstream module), a global random direction, a random direction inside slot 0, and the read direction itself (a pure rescale). Because removing a write also changes the read's MAGNITUDE, the component of d_X orthogonal to hn is reported beside the raw one and the cosine is recorded. tf_round2_review.py routing -> R1_routing_fairness.
R1_is_the_routing_measurement_architectu.result_matched_displacement: At a 10% read displacement along layer-0 attention's own direction (orthogonalised), the KL is LARGEST IN THE PLAIN MODEL: vanilla 0.0270 / 0.0172 / 0.0163 (seeds 0/1/2) against slots 0.0203 / 0.0140 / 0.0160, bandwidth 0.0124 / 0.0114 / 0.0189, predicate 0.0132 / 0.0146 / 0.0125, codebook 0.0121 / 0.0127 / 0.0138, shrink 0.0108 / 0.0099 / 0.0096. Against a random direction of the same size, vanilla amplifies layer-0 attention's direction 5.8-8.1x, more than any variant (slots 3.7-5.2, bandwidth 3.0-5.0, predicate 5.3-5.6, shrink 2.5-3.0, codebook 1.3-1.5). The magnitude confound is absent in vanilla by measurement: |cos(d_A0, read)| = 0.001 there (0.33-0.50 in the variants), so vanilla's number is pure direction sensitivity.
R1_is_the_routing_measurement_architectu.result_consistency_check: The local gain measured this way PREDICTS the original deletion number in the plain model. Quadratic extrapolation KL = gain * readrel^2 from the eps = 0.1 probe to vanilla's actual 0.32% / 0.25% / 0.18% displacement gives 2.73e-5 / 1.06e-5 / 5.01e-6 against measured 2.42e-5 / 9.80e-6 / 4.66e-6 -- within 8-13%. So the plain model's ~zero routing KL is exactly what its ordinary local sensitivity produces at its tiny displacement; nothing extra is being shut. (For the variants the same extrapolation over-predicts by 1.2-3x because a 60% displacement is past the quadratic regime, which makes the comparison conservative in the variants' favour and does not change the conclusion.)
R1_is_the_routing_measurement_architectu.verdict: SURVIVES AS A CAUSAL FACT, RETRACTED AS A MECHANISM. What is transmitted really is ~0 in vanilla and 0.07-0.15 nats in the variants -- that is a property of the trained models and it stands. What must be withdrawn is the gloss that the plain model's layer 1 is BLIND to the channel or that the variants OPENED something in weight space: per unit of read displacement the plain model is the most sensitive of the six to layer-0 attention's direction. The correct statement is a magnitude statement: the plain model renormalises its own layer-0 attention write down to 0.3% of layer 1's read, so a fully-sensitive channel carries nothing; per-slot RMSNorm removes that option and forces the write to a quarter of the read, at which point the same sensitivity delivers 0.1 nats. This is the 'removes the option to collapse' framing that FINDING 11 section 4 already used -- it is now the ONLY framing the data supports, and section 1's 'the plain model shuts the path, every variant opens it' has been rewritten accordingly.
R1_is_the_routing_measurement_architectu.second_objection_the_route_split_could_b: If deleting A0 from layer-1's read is a 60% perturbation, of course the induction score dies -- a big enough perturbation kills everything. Specificity control, already in the data and now read out: the same intervention removes 117% of the induction score in slots but only 15% of the BAG score (the order-free component of the same battery); shrink 153% vs 5%; codebook 124% vs 40%; bandwidth 111% vs 54%. Induction dies while the bag effect largely survives, so the route is content-specific and section 2 stands. Bandwidth is the weakest case and is quoted with its bag figure.
R1_is_the_routing_measurement_architectu.third_objection_vanillas_own_route_fract: vanilla at d2 w128 has route fractions of -1.11, -13.8 and +7.42 across seeds -- meaningless, because the denominator (its own induction score) is null. FINDING 11's route table correctly uses vanilla at WIDTH 256 (baseline +0.084, read route -0.005, MLP route +1.435) and never the width-128 cell; verified, no change needed, and the width-128 fractions are now explicitly marked undefined.

R2_what_else_differs_between_plain_and_v.objection: With the learning-rate falsifier dead (vanilla is null at Muon 0.01, 0.02 and 0.04), induction-at-half-the-width could still come from something other than the architecture: initialisation scale, an effective per-parameter-block learning rate, embedding capacity, or the number of trainable directions the run actually uses.
R2_what_else_differs_between_plain_and_v.measurement: Every arm re-instantiated at its own config and seed (TinyBilin seeds the RNG in __init__, so the init is bit-reproducible) and diffed against its trained weights: per-block init RMS, relative distance travelled ||W_final - W_init||/||W_init||, and the participation-ratio effective rank of both the init and the update. tf_round2_review.py optim -> R2_what_else_differs.
R2_what_else_differs_between_plain_and_v.initialisation_scale: vanilla, slots, shrink and the write-init-only arm have BIT-IDENTICAL init RMS in every read matrix (c_q 0.0512, c_k 0.0509, c_v 0.0511, Left 0.0510, embedding 0.0200). The only init difference is the decoder: 0.0000 (vanilla) vs 0.0172 (variants) -- exactly the confound the writeinit_only arm isolates, and that arm is null on induction (-0.0095) with the path still shut (3.5e-6). bandwidth/predicate/codebook do init smaller (0.0454-0.0457) because their stream is 160 wide, but slots matches vanilla exactly and shows the full effect. REFUTED as an explanation.
R2_what_else_differs_between_plain_and_v.effective_learning_rate_per_block: Two independent reasons. (a) Structural: the body matrices are trained by Muon, whose update is orthogonalised, so the per-step update size is set by the learning rate and is invariant to the gradient's scale; the embedding and sub-2D parameters are on AdamW, which is also approximately scale-free. A per-block gradient-magnitude difference therefore cannot become a per-block step-size difference. (b) Measured, and the sign is the wrong way round for the objection: vanilla travels FURTHER from init at layer-0 attention than slots does (c_q 12.88 vs 6.88, c_k 14.74 vs 5.88 relative), so the plain model moves its first attention block MORE and still does not induct. REFUTED.
R2_what_else_differs_between_plain_and_v.embedding_capacity: slots has vanilla's embedding exactly (8192 x 128, 1,048,576 parameters, identical init) and inducts at +0.097 +- 0.028 over three seeds. The utilisation is the same too: the effective rank of the embedding update is 0.806-0.839 of its maximum in every arm. The wider-stream variants are separately controlled by the _slot32 arms, which pin the embedding back to vanilla's and keep the effect (bandwidth +0.0962, predicate +2.4597). REFUTED.
R2_what_else_differs_between_plain_and_v.number_of_trainable_directions_used: effective rank of the update, as a fraction of the maximum: layer-0 c_q 0.443 (vanilla) vs 0.552 (slots), layer-0 c_v 0.717 vs 0.623, layer-1 c_q 0.571 vs 0.567, Left 0.950 vs 0.934, embedding 0.838 vs 0.806. The two models use the same number of directions to within a few percent and the ordering flips block to block. NOT AN EXPLANATION.
R2_what_else_differs_between_plain_and_v.what_does_remain: The masked-decoder arms (slots, shrink) have a much lower-rank decoder update -- erank(delta)/max 0.24 for c_proj and Down against vanilla's 0.66 and 0.96 -- which is the write mask by construction (32 live rows of 128), i.e. arithmetic, not a finding. Recorded as such.
R2_what_else_differs_between_plain_and_v.verdict: SURVIVES the objection: none of the four alternatives separates the arms, and two of them (init scale, distance travelled) point the wrong way. Combined with the learning-rate arms at 0.01/0.02/0.04 and the writeinit_only / nolasso mechanism arms, the induction difference is attributable to the write partition plus per-slot RMSNorm.

R3a_the_lasso_prunes_nothing.objection: 'The in-loss group lasso empties no slot' is reported as an architectural promise only half kept. But 3e-5 was inherited from another program at another scale. If the penalty is numerically negligible against the cross-entropy, the finding says nothing about slot architectures -- it says our coefficient was too small, and an unflattering claim about our own design is being made on a configuration accident.
R3a_the_lasso_prunes_nothing.measurement_1_arithmetic: The penalty evaluated at the trained checkpoints (tf_round2_review.py lasso -> R3a_lasso_coefficient): at 3e-5 the penalty term is 1682.8, so coeff*penalty = 0.0505 nats, 1.07% of the 4.74 held CE -- NOT negligible. And it bites: the same quantity at the no-lasso arm is 2706.0, so the lasso has shrunk the total group norm by 38% without emptying a single group. Replicated at seeds 1 and 2 (1690.6, 1668.8; 1.07%, 1.06%).
R3a_the_lasso_prunes_nothing.measurement_2_the_retrain: slots retrained at group-lasso coefficients 3e-4, 3e-3 and 3e-2 (10x, 100x and 1000x the reported 3e-5) and put through the same tf_interp3 pass (tf_round2_train.log). The penalty is fully effective at SHRINKING: the total group norm over the 14 read matrices falls 2706.0 (no lasso) -> 1682.8 (3e-5) -> 375.7 (3e-4) -> 37.6 (3e-3) -> 2.94 (3e-2), a factor of 920. It never SELECTS: mean_live_slots_per_read stays at 4.00 of 4 at every coefficient, all 56 slot groups stay above 1% of their matrix's mass at every coefficient, and the smallest single group share only falls from 0.145 to 0.017. What breaks first is the model, not a slot: held CE 4.7607 / 4.7418 / 4.7273 / 4.9633 / 5.2195 and induction +0.0836 / +0.1129 / +0.1424 / -0.0324 / -0.0163 (the last two at or below their own power floors, i.e. the induction the architecture buys is destroyed before any slot is emptied).
R3a_the_lasso_prunes_nothing.verdict: SURVIVES, and is STRENGTHENED. 'The in-loss group lasso prunes nothing' is not a coefficient artifact: over three decades of coefficient, with the total group norm driven down by a factor of 920, not one of the 56 slot groups is ever emptied, while the cross-entropy degrades by 0.22-0.48 nats and the induction the architecture buys is destroyed. At this size the penalty shrinks all groups proportionally instead of selecting among them. One incidental correction in the mechanism's favour: 3e-5 was NOT the best coefficient -- 3e-4 is better on both CE (4.7273 vs 4.7418) and induction (+0.1424 vs +0.1129) -- so the primary slots arm is quoted at a slightly suboptimal setting, which makes its 0.091-nat CE cost against vanilla an overestimate (0.076 at 3e-4). The pruning conclusion is unchanged. Also corrected: the write-up says '28 read matrices'; the measured object is 14 read matrices per model (7 per block x 2 blocks) carrying 56 slot groups.

R3b_the_codebook_uses_all_256_atoms_at_2.objection: Two halves, and both are unflattering to our own design, so both are under-scrutinised. (i) 'All 256 atoms used near-uniformly' could be an EMA-codebook artifact rather than a fact about the activations. (ii) '22-39% injected error' is quoted from a relative residual measured over the FULL module input, but only one or two of the four slots are ever quantised, so the unquantised slots dilute it.
R3b_the_codebook_uses_all_256_atoms_at_2.measurement: The model's OWN matching-pursuit quantiser at the model's own k (4 steps at the attention input, 2 at the MLP input) run against four dictionaries on the same activations, fit on a train half and scored on a held half: the trained codebook, k-means at 64/256/1024, the random unit dictionary the model was initialised from, and a same-budget continuous alternative (PCA to k dimensions). tf_round2_review.py codebook -> R3b_codebook_flatness, seeds 0 and 1.
R3b_the_codebook_uses_all_256_atoms_at_2.result_the_flatness_is_the_data: k-means -- which is free to be as unequal as it likes and is fit for exactly this purpose -- is FLATTER than the trained codebook, not sharper: usage entropy 0.98 of maximum at K=256 against the trained codebook's 0.83, and 202 atoms for 90% of assignments against 111. The near-uniform dictionary is a property of the activation distribution. Registered prediction P4's sub-clause ('fewer than half the atoms carry 90%') is refuted for the right reason.
R3b_the_codebook_uses_all_256_atoms_at_2.result_the_error_number_is_wrong_twice: On the slots actually quantised the relative error is 0.77-0.85, not 0.22-0.39; the published figure is the full-width residual diluted by the three unquantised slots. And the dictionary is badly under-trained: a k-means dictionary of the SAME 256 atoms, with the same matching pursuit at the same k, reaches 0.43-0.51 -- roughly twice as good -- while the trained codebook (0.846 at consumer 1) is no better than the RANDOM unit dictionary it was initialised from (0.816). A same-budget PCA to k dimensions also beats it (0.70-0.77). So the codebook fails the README's 'beat a same-parameter-count alternative' test.
R3b_the_codebook_uses_all_256_atoms_at_2.verdict: SPLIT. The flatness claim SURVIVES and is strengthened (the flatness is in the activations, not in the mechanism). The error claim is RETRACTED and restated: the per-quantised-slot relative error is 0.77-0.85, and the EMA codebook is additionally about 2x worse than a properly fit dictionary of the same size and no better than its own random initialisation -- so the codebook arm's 0.097 nats of CE cost buys a dictionary that is both flat AND under-trained. The write-up now says the mechanism is under-trained at this size rather than implying the discreteness itself was given a fair run.
R3b_the_codebook_uses_all_256_atoms_at_2.consequence_for_the_headline: None. The codebook arm's routing and induction numbers are unaffected; this concerns only the legibility claim in FINDING 11 section 6.

R3c_the_shrink_projections_are_near_full.objection: 'Near full rank for the width they are given (entropy rank 62.2 of 64 at block 1, 30.9 of 32 at the readout), so the floor is doing the compressing, not the model' is an ENTROPY-RANK statement about a spectrum. Entropy rank is not causal: a flat spectrum is compatible with the small directions doing no work. Condemning our own mechanism on a spectral statistic is the 'arithmetic dressed as a finding' failure mode running in reverse.
R3c_the_shrink_projections_are_near_full.measurement: Each remnant projection truncated to its top-r singular directions, r = 1..full, scored as held KL from the untruncated model with everything downstream recomputed; beside it the same rank budget spent on a RANDOM subspace, which is the same-parameter-count alternative the README demands. Three seeds. tf_round2_review.py shrink -> R3c_shrink_causal_rank.
R3c_the_shrink_projections_are_near_full.result_block_1_remnant_64_wide: Causally full rank, confirming the spectral claim: truncating to 32 of 64 still costs 0.28-0.33 nats, to 48 costs 0.12-0.16, and only the full 64 reaches 0. And the particular subspace matters -- a RANDOM 64-dimensional subspace of the 128-wide stream costs 0.45-0.50 nats where the model's own costs 0 -- so the model has selected a specific 64-dimensional summary even though it has not made it low rank.
R3c_the_shrink_projections_are_near_full.result_readout_remnant_32_wide: The claim is WRONG here. Truncating this projection to rank ONE costs 0.022-0.023 nats, i.e. 31 of its 32 directions are causally worthless, and the whole projection is worth at most ~0.023 nats (a random rank-1 subspace costs 0.023-0.026, statistically the same). Entropy rank 30.9 of 32 described a spectrum that carries almost nothing.
R3c_the_shrink_projections_are_near_full.verdict: SPLIT: SURVIVES at the block-1 remnant (and is strengthened by the random-subspace control), RETRACTED at the readout remnant. FINDING 11 section 6 now reads: the shrinking channel does find a specific 64-dimensional summary for block 1 and genuinely uses all 64 of its directions, and its 32-wide readout remnant is causally rank one and nearly inert. Quoting entropy rank alone for both was the error.

R3d_the_wiring_tilt_claim.objection: Section 6 keeps the wiring table as 'informative by its tilt' (layer 1's queries and keys put 0.40-0.47 of their group mass on slot 0 against ~0.20 on the MLP's slot, values only 0.11-0.14) and says the tilt agrees with the causal answer. After R1 the causal answer has changed, so the agreement needs re-checking.
R3d_the_wiring_tilt_claim.assessment: The tilt is a statement about which slots layer 1's read matrices weight, and R1 does not touch it: what R1 retracts is the inference from the DELETION KL to a weight-space claim about vanilla, not the variants' weight shares. The tilt remains an honest weight-space observation with the caveat already attached (the token remnant is full width, so mass on an unwritten slot is reading the embedding). It is downgraded from 'agrees with the causal result' to 'consistent with it', because R1's matched-displacement probe shows the plain model's read weights are at least as tilted toward layer-0 attention's direction and it has no partition to show it in.

R4_what_rests_on_one_seed_one_probe_or_o.found_by_this_review_and_NOT_previously_: CODEBOOK FAILS ITS OWN POWER FLOOR AT SEED 2: induction +0.0228 against a 3-SE floor of 0.0249 (0.9x). Seeds 0 and 1 are +0.0540 (6.3x) and +0.0358 (4.2x). The claim 'all five variants acquire induction at width 128' is therefore 3/3 for slots, bandwidth, predicate and shrink and 2/3 for codebook. The natural-text swap does replicate for codebook at all three seeds (+0.168 / +0.142 / +0.140, t = 8.3-8.7, against vanilla's +0.100 / +0.092 / +0.117, t = 5.8-6.8), so the arm is not null -- but the synthetic headline must be quoted as 2 of 3 and is.
R4_what_rests_on_one_seed_one_probe_or_o.still_one_seed_after_this_review: NOTHING load-bearing. What remains at two seeds rather than three: the matched-embedding slot32 arms and the learning-rate arms (both one-directional controls that agree at both seeds), and the per-variant DEPTH-1 matched nulls for the natural-text swap probe, which were seed 0 only and are now seeds 0 and 1 for all six variants (tf_round2_trainb.log; vanilla 0.0670/0.0694, slots 0.0842/0.0872, bandwidth 0.1022/0.0934, predicate 1.5306/1.5406, codebook 0.0866/0.0856, shrink 0.0815/0.0850 -- seed spreads of 0.0007-0.0062, far below the depth-2 excesses of 0.04-0.12). A latent seed-mixing bug in the aggregation was fixed while doing this: tf_variant_compare.py assigned `d1[variant] = ...` inside its loop and would have silently kept only the LAST depth-1 seed found; it now averages over all of them and reports the spread. Everything else in the table is at three seeds. The remaining limitations are listed in RESULTS.md section 10 and are limitations, not to-dos.
R4_what_rests_on_one_seed_one_probe_or_o.one_ablation_method: Every knockout in the table is already quoted as a [zero, resample] RANGE, and the review adds a third, independent intervention family for the routing claim (the matched-displacement directional probe in R1), which is what overturned the mechanism. The per-head ranking is explicitly reported as not surviving the switch from zeroing to resampling, which is the correct treatment.
R4_what_rests_on_one_seed_one_probe_or_o.one_probe: Induction is measured by two probes that disagree in construction (a planted synthetic oracle with its own power floor, and a bag-preserving swap on natural text with a depth-1 matched null) and they agree on every arm's sign. The content-spectrum claim rests on ONE statistic and is handled in R5.
R4_what_rests_on_one_seed_one_probe_or_o.verdict: SURVIVES for slots, bandwidth, predicate and shrink; WEAKENED for codebook (2 of 3 seeds on the synthetic probe, 3 of 3 on the natural-text probe), and the write-up now says so.
R4_what_rests_on_one_seed_one_probe_or_o.control_arms_replicated_by_this_review: Round 1 had every mechanism and matched-parameter arm at seed 0 only. Retrained and re-analysed through the same pipeline (tf_round2_train.log): write-init-only at seeds 0/1/2 -- induction -0.0095 / -0.0117 / -0.0025, every one BELOW its own power floor, routing 3.5e-6 / 5.6e-6 / 3.4e-6, so the nonzero decoder init explains none of the effect at three seeds; no-lasso at seeds 0/1/2 -- induction +0.0836 / +0.0999 / +0.0442 (all above floor), routing 0.483 / 0.469 / 0.474, so the partition plus per-slot norm IS the mechanism at three seeds; matched-embedding slot32 at seeds 0/1 -- bandwidth +0.0962 / +0.0797, predicate +2.4597 / +2.5189, routing 0.27-0.50, so the extra embedding is not the cause at two seeds; the learning-rate falsifier at seeds 0/1 -- vanilla -0.0180 / -0.0013 at Muon 0.01 and -0.0142 / -0.0117 at 0.04, null everywhere. R5_the_content_null_result_has_an_uncali.objection: 'No variant moves content off its spectral null -- 0.98 to 1.00 of the same-shape random-factored null in all six' is a NULL RESULT, and the README's standing failure mode says a null result is worth nothing until the detector is shown to detect a planted effect of known size. The selection side reading 0.19-0.36 is in-sample evidence that the statistic is not pinned at 1, but it is not a calibration.
R5_the_content_null_result_has_an_uncali.measurement: Bilinear content tensors with a genuinely low-dimensional input dependence planted at each variant's own tensor shape (the Left and Right factors restricted to an r-dimensional input subspace, r = 2/4/8/16/32 of a 128- or 160-wide stream), scored by the identical entropy-rank-over-null statistic against the identical shape-matched null. tf_round2_review.py content -> R5_content_detector_power.
R5_the_content_null_result_has_an_uncali.result: The detector has power, but only against strongly low-dimensional content: planted input rank 2 reads 0.02-0.09 of the null, rank 4 reads 0.07-0.30, rank 8 reads 0.27-0.83, rank 16 reads 0.80-0.96, and rank 32 reads 0.95-0.99 -- indistinguishable from the model's own 0.98-1.00.
R5_the_content_null_result_has_an_uncali.verdict: WEAKENED, and the claim is re-quoted with its detection threshold. What the measurement supports is: the MLP content tensor is not confined to fewer than about 8-16 of the stream's 128-160 input directions, in any of the six architectures. It does NOT support 'content has no structure' or 'content is exactly as flat as random'. FINDING 11 section 5 item 4 has been rewritten to state the threshold.

R6_the_two_ce_conventions_and_the_bits_p.objection: The README makes bits/byte mandatory for any cross-tokenizer number, and round 1 records two CE conventions (held CE at T=512 over 1500 sequences vs the ladder's _model_ce at T=256 over 96). A reviewer should check neither rule has slipped in the consolidated table.
R6_the_two_ce_conventions_and_the_bits_p.check: Every arm in the slice uses the same corpus and the same tokenizer (trained byte-level BPE, V=8192), so nats/token is the correct within-tokenizer unit; bits/byte is carried beside it in Table A and Table B anyway (vanilla 1.7853 +- 0.0029, predicate 1.6854 +- 0.0008, codebook 1.8268 +- 0.0021) and the two orderings agree exactly. The two CE conventions are both present, labelled, and never mixed in a single row.

R7_the_predicate_headline_is_a_handover_.objection: predicate's +2.64 induction is 31x the largest induction this program has ever measured and is 85-138x its power floor. That is not the model learning a circuit: MATCH_prev[i,j] = 1[tok_{j-1} == tok_i] IS an induction head, supplied as an architectural kernel. Presenting it in the same column as slots' +0.11 invites exactly the wrong reading.
R7_the_predicate_headline_is_a_handover_.assessment: Round 1 already declared this (C8) and the write-up says it. The reviewer's addition is that it must be visible in the TABLE, not only in the prose, because tables travel without their paragraphs. Confirmed by the ablation: zeroing the 16 previous-token match scalars removes 98.7% (seed 0) and 99.1% (seed 1) of it and zeroing all named terms lands on vanilla's null; the learned bilinear branches contribute none of it.
R7_the_predicate_headline_is_a_handover_.verdict: SURVIVES as a capability claim, and the consolidated table now flags the predicate row as architecturally supplied.

R8_a_latent_bug_the_review_found_in_the_.how_it_surfaced: The review tried to run a PARTITION DOSE-RESPONSE arm -- n_slots = 2 at depth 2, expected to sit between n_slots = 1 (vanilla plus init, null) and n_slots = 4 (full effect). It trained without complaint and reached CE 4.8898.
R8_a_latent_bug_the_review_found_in_the_.the_bug: TinyBilin builds its write masks with `wm[k, slot*k : slot*(k+1)] = 1.0` for k = 0..2*depth-1. A python slice past the end of a row is legal and empty, so with n_slots < 2*depth every module beyond the last slot gets an ALL-ZERO write mask. At n_slots = 2, depth 2 the write masks are [64, 64, 0, 0]: the whole second block -- its attention AND its MLP -- writes nothing into the stream, and nothing anywhere reports it. A second consequence downstream: tf_interp3's live-row selection indexes rows slot*k .. slot*(k+1), which for that config runs off the end of the tensor (index 248 of 128) and raised, which is how it was caught.
R8_a_latent_bug_the_review_found_in_the_.blast_radius: ZERO for the slice. Every arm in the comparison uses n_slots = 2*depth (4) or n_slots = 1 (the writeinit_only reduction, where the mask is all ones by a separate branch). All 65 real checkpoints load under the new guard; only the two invalid dose-response arms fail.
R8_a_latent_bug_the_review_found_in_the_.fix: an assertion in tf_model.TinyBilin that no write mask is empty, naming the offending modules. The two n_slots=2 arms are DISCARDED and the dose-response is not reported.
